_readme: Corrections applied on top of the upstream API specification.
Every entry was decided from evidence, not from guesswork:
(a) a live call against https://api.tino.vn, or
(b) the request shape Tino's production client actually sends.
'remove'       endpoints the live API answers with 404 {"error":["invalid method"]}
'patch'        corrected paths, auth flags, query params, notes
'add'          endpoints in production use but absent from the specification
'verifiedLive' endpoints whose response shape was captured from a real call

domains.getTldForm.notes: {id} is the TLD product id returned by cart.listDomainTlds (e.g. 1298 for .io.vn), not the id of a registered domain.

languages.getBillingCycleLabels.summary: Billing cycle labels in the active language

fields.name: query
fields.description: Search keyword (service domain, invoice number, ticket subject, ...)

account.search.notes: The search keyword goes in the request body as {"query": "..."}, not in the path.

cart.order.notes: The single entry point for placing an order. It accepts several items of any product type in one call — hosting, VPS, domains, SSL — so the per-product and per-domain order routes are not needed. Preview the price first with cart.quote, which takes the same payload and creates nothing.

cart.quote.notes: Price preview for a cart.order payload. Returns the subtotal, tax, discounts and recurring amounts without creating an order or an invoice.

cart.orderProduct.notes: Legacy single-product form. Use cart.order instead — it is the supported way to place an order and handles multiple items in one call.

domains.order.notes: Domains are ordered through cart.order together with any other item. This route remains for the standalone domain flow.

certificates.order.notes: Certificates are ordered through cart.order together with any other item. This route remains for the standalone certificate flow.

security.addIpAccess.notes: The first rule switches the account into whitelist mode: every address that is not listed is refused, including the one you are calling from. Add your own address before adding any other, and remove it last.

vms.createSnapshot.notes: The snapshot name is generated by the platform (A<unix-timestamp>); a name sent in the request is ignored. Read it back from vms.listSnapshots before deleting.

support.createTicket.notes: Returns the new ticket number as {"ticket": 690686} — the field is `ticket`, not `ticket_number`. Use it as the {number} path parameter of the other ticket calls.

account.getDetails.notes: The response now carries verify.phone (bool) and a phone block {status, verified_at}. status is one of verified | unverified | taken_by_other | missing. Note that the top-level update_required is about the profile (national id, address), not the phone.

auth.login.notes: The response now carries verify.phone (bool) and a phone block {status, verified_at}. status is one of verified | unverified | taken_by_other | missing. Note that the top-level update_required is about the profile (national id, address), not the phone.

auth.loginSso.notes: The response now carries verify.phone (bool) and a phone block {status, verified_at}. status is one of verified | unverified | taken_by_other | missing. Note that the top-level update_required is about the profile (national id, address), not the phone.

auth.verifyLoginOtp.notes: The response now carries verify.phone (bool) and a phone block {status, verified_at}. status is one of verified | unverified | taken_by_other | missing. Note that the top-level update_required is about the profile (national id, address), not the phone.

auth.requestLoginOtp.notes: via reports the delivery channel. It falls back to email when the account's phone number is already verified by a different account, so an OTP is never sent to a SIM the account holder may not control.

account.updateDetails.notes: Changing phonenumber clears the phone verification: phone.status returns to unverified and the old number is released for another account to claim.

auth.signup.notes: Rejects a duplicate phone number with phone_invalid, phone_already_verified or phone_already_used, so one number registers exactly one account.

add.name: requestOtp
add.description: Send a one-time code to prove the account owner holds the SIM. Tries Zalo ZNS first and falls back to SMS when the number has no Zalo account, so no channel configuration is needed. Omit phonenumber to verify the number already on the account. Accounts that have already verified a number are refused with already_verified — change the number through PUT /details first, which clears the previous verification.

fields.name: phonenumber
fields.description: Number to verify. Defaults to the one on the account.

add.notes: The response reports the channel actually used in `via` (`zalo` or `sms`). Email is never used here: it proves control of a mailbox, not possession of the SIM. The code lasts 300 seconds, may be resent after 60 seconds, at most 3 times, and is destroyed after 5 wrong attempts. Both channels fail -> otp_send_failed.

add.name: verify
add.description: Confirm the code sent by phone.requestOtp. On success the number is written to the profile when it changed, and ownership of it is claimed for this account. No new token is issued — the current session continues.
add.notes: Returns {success, phone:{status, verified_at}}. A phone belongs to exactly one account: claiming is guarded by a unique index, so a race loses cleanly with phone_already_verified. The channel that carried the code is recorded against the account as the proof of ownership.

add.name: listDomains
add.description: Up to 200 .vn domains whose status is `auction`, sorted by night F ascending (night F is when VNNIC is expected to delete the domain). Each entry carries the round schedule `rounds[]`, `current_round`, `open_now` (bids are accepted only when true), the highest bid `price` (null before the first bid), the next minimum bid `min_bid` and the bid count `bids`. No `my` key here. Send no Authorization header: an expired token can make a 200 answer carry an `error` key, so judge success by the HTTP status and `success`.
add.notes: Rounds default to three, 20:00-20:30 on F-4, F-3 and F-2, but the count and the times are configuration: always render `rounds[]`, which may hold `skipped` rounds. Every successful answer carries `price_note`: bids exclude the VAT charged on the auction fee. Money is VND as a JSON number and may carry `.0`; display it as an integer. Times are ISO 8601 in +07:00; night F is `YYYY-MM-DD`. Bids, balance, orders and invoices belong to the main account, so a contact shares them.

add.name: getDomain
add.summary: Get one backorder auction with the caller's position
add.description: The same domain object as backorder.listDomains plus `my`: the caller's best bid in the current round (`best`), its `rank` (1 is highest), whether it is `leading`, and whether the caller is `banned` from this domain for winning an earlier round without paying. An unknown id answers HTTP 404 {success:false, error:"not_found"}.

pathParams.name: id
pathParams.description: Backorder id, the `id` of an entry in backorder.listDomains

add.notes: There is no push channel: while `open_now` is true, re-read about every 5 seconds; those reads count toward the route's rate limit (HTTP 429). Trust `open_now` over a local countdown to `close_at`. Every successful answer carries `price_note`: bids exclude the VAT charged on the auction fee. Money is VND as a JSON number and may carry `.0`; display it as an integer. Times are ISO 8601 in +07:00; night F is `YYYY-MM-DD`. Bids, balance, orders and invoices belong to the main account, so a contact shares them.

add.name: placeBid
add.summary: Place a bid on a backorder auction
add.description: Bid in the open round. The bid must be at least `min_bid`: the start price plus the bid step for the round's first bid, then the highest bid plus the step, so a bid equal to the current price is always too low. The account balance must reach `min_balance` and `balance_ratio` percent of the bid; it is checked, never held or debited. The current leader cannot bid again. Success answers HTTP 200 {success, ok, round_no, price, min_bid}. A refusal answers HTTP 422 {success:false, ok:false, error, message, min_bid}; `min_bid` there is meaningful only with `too_low`. Codes, checked in this order: domain_closed (also for an unknown id), held, not_open, closed, banned, already_top, bad_amount, too_low, min_balance, balance_ratio.

pathParams.name: id
pathParams.description: Backorder id, the `id` of an entry in backorder.listDomains

fields.name: amount
fields.description: Bid in whole VND, from min_bid up to 9999999999. A string of digits is also accepted; no thousands separators.

add.notes: Rows are locked while a bid is written, so two bids in the same second are serialised and the second sees the new price. Send JSON only with `Content-Type: application/json`, otherwise the server reads no parameter and answers bad_amount. Rounds close a few minutes after `close_at`: the highest bidder wins an order and an invoice, which HostBill may settle from the balance at once when CreditAutoApply is on. Every successful answer carries `price_note`: bids exclude the VAT charged on the auction fee. Money is VND as a JSON number and may carry `.0`; display it as an integer. Times are ISO 8601 in +07:00; night F is `YYYY-MM-DD`. Bids, balance, orders and invoices belong to the main account, so a contact shares them.

add.name: listMyRounds
add.summary: List the backorder rounds the caller bid in
add.description: Up to 100 rounds the caller bid in, most recently created first (newer domains first, later rounds first within a domain); sort client-side for any other order. Each carries `round_status`, `my_best` and `result`: leading, outbid, closing, won, forfeited, cancelled or lost. A `won` round adds `price`, `order_id`, `invoice_id`, `invoice_total` (VAT included), `pay_deadline` and `backorder_result`. Offer payment only while `round_status` is `awaiting_payment`.
add.notes: For a won round read the first match: round_status awaiting_payment means pay `invoice_id` before `pay_deadline`; domain_status won means captured; lost or cancelled means refunded to the balance; error means staff are handling it; paid or queued means waiting for the capture night. `backorder_result` does not change when staff cancel a job, so always read it with `domain_status`. Every successful answer carries `price_note`: bids exclude the VAT charged on the auction fee. Money is VND as a JSON number and may carry `.0`; display it as an integer. Times are ISO 8601 in +07:00; night F is `YYYY-MM-DD`. Bids, balance, orders and invoices belong to the main account, so a contact shares them.
